method: Continuous linear-program relaxation over aggregate test metadata capacities by family/gana/lakara/grammar cell. No test model answers or per-question outcomes are loaded. Only aggregate allocations are saved; no final membership is selected.

reference_details.adanta: Pilot04 56/64 source-supported broad cell. Refinement uses post-hoc phonological/tense slices with n11,13,17,23 and large uncertainty; pilot05 is pending fresh-tuple confirmation.
reference_details.background03: 175/175 after current scope restrictions and sensitivity omission of the unresolved stim disagreement. This is a point estimate, not certainty or a new independent measurement.

diversity_interpretation: No numerical class cap, family cap or equal tense quota is attributed to the user. Unrestricted cases expose best concentration. Spread cases illustrate broad coverage using >=1% in each available gana and lakara, <=25% aorist, and varying family/class caps. Floors are modest design choices and should not be mistaken for exact uniformity requirements.
limits: The relaxation permits fractional tasks, so it is optimistic relative to an actual integer panel.
Fixed empirical cell rates are not known test accuracies. Adaptive discovery, small cells and family correlation make these bounds unsuitable for proving statistical impossibility.
The counted predicate union is not the full search universe. New source-clean mechanisms may change the frontier.
Metadata source scope is screened by the shared policy plus local exclusions; representative controls do not fully certify every potential test paradigm.
